statement.p: Consider the graphs below, which give m(x) in the left graph, in black, and n(x) in the right graph, in blue. Both functions have a sharp corner at x = 50.
Let h(x) = n(m(x)). Find a point x where h'(x) = 1.96.

solution.p: Since the chain rule gives h'(x) = n'(m(x)) m'(x) = 1.96 we must find values a and x such that a=m(x) and n'(a) m'(x)= 1.96.

Calculating slopes from the graph of n gives n'(a) = 1.4 for 0 \lt a \lt 50 and n'(a) = 0.6 for 50 \lt a \lt 100. Similarly calculating slopes from the graph of m gives m'(x) = -1.4 for 0 \lt x \lt 50 and m'(x) = 1.4 for 50 \lt x \lt 100.

The only values of the derivative n' are 1.4 and 0.6 and the only values of the derivative m' are -1.4 and 1.4. In order to have n'(a) m'(x)= 1.96 we must therefore have n'(a)=1.4 and m'(x) = 1.4. Thus 0 \lt a \lt 50 and 50 \lt x \lt 100.

Now a=m(x) and from the graph of m we see that 0 \lt m(x) \lt 50 for 35.71 \lt x \lt 64.29. The two conditions on x we have found are both satisfied when 50 \lt x \lt 64.29. Thus h'(x)= 1.96 for all x in the interval 50 \lt x \lt 64.29. The question asks for just one of these x values (any will work).
